scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Turn on a VPN, and websites think you're somewhere else. Your Wi-Fi can't see where you're going either. How?

scenes.name: normal
scenes.text: Normally, your internet provider or the Wi-Fi network can see which websites you connect to, even if the pages themselves are encrypted.

scenes.name: tunnel
scenes.text: A VPN app creates an encrypted tunnel from your device to a VPN server. All your traffic goes inside it.

scenes.name: server
scenes.text: The VPN server then contacts websites for you. So websites see the server's address and location, not yours.

scenes.name: see
scenes.text: Your Wi-Fi or provider only sees scrambled data going to the VPN. But the VPN company itself can see where you go, so trust matters.

scenes.name: limits
scenes.text: A VPN isn't full anonymity. Logged in accounts, cookies and your browser can still identify you.

scenes.name: india
scenes.text: In India, rules from 2022 require VPN providers to keep certain records about their users.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Encrypt, tunnel, relay, trust. Privacy with limits. Follow for more on how things really work.
